newsitem.title: CANADA: Cdn Fracmaster CEO Balm sells stake, resigns.
newsitem.headline: Cdn Fracmaster CEO Balm sells stake, resigns.

text.p: Oil services firm Canadian Fracmaster Ltd said on Wednesday that Chairman and Chief Executive Alfred Balm would sell his whole 67.5 percent stake, or 28.9 million shares, and resign as chief executive.
Fracmaster said it will file a preliminary short form prospectus on August 13 outlining the proposed sale by way of a secondary offering of common shares through instalment receipts.
The offering, underwritten by Newcrest Capital Inc and a syndicate, will be made only in Canada and expected to close in September.
President Les Margetak will take over the role of chief executive after the transaction is finished.
Alfred Balm said in a press release that "the Company is realizing significant growth under its continuing management. I believe it is time for me to retire from my role as chief executive officer."
The firm, buoyed by rising revenue from North American and Russian services, has seen its stock price climb since October and reach all-time highs since it went public in 1993.

Speculation had already swirled in Canada's oil patch whether Balm, a Geneva-based businessman, would sell part or all of his interest. The company did not say whether he would also resign as chairman.
At Fracmaster's closing share price of C$19.25 on Tuesday, Balm's holding would be worth about C$550 million.
